items: Free preview has its own home page: the free lessons, the solved 2019 paper and the unlock button, instead of the study plan
Website: 'Try it free' is now the first thing on the code page
Ask a doubt is now only in the course owner's copy
Free preview on the website: 4 full lessons and the solved IDO 2019 paper without a code; other lessons show 🔒 Unlock

Your own study plan: pick the day you start and the date you expect the exam, and every lesson, revision day and mock is fitted between them (new users are asked on first open; everyone else: Progress → Study plan → Set my dates)
Short on time? Lessons are packed more per day; more time? Extra revision and mock days are added. The day before the exam is always a light day.
Bengali names for the two new lessons: 98 terms (sarees, silk, handloom bodies, leather, petrochemicals, parks…) now in the glossary, Bengali flashcards and the বাংলা toggle

New lesson: Sarees, handloom and silk of Bengal — every saree with its Bengali name, district, fibre, what makes it different and GI year (Tant, Shantipuri, Dhaniakhali, Begampuri, Baluchari, Swarnachari, Garad, Korial, Tangail, Jamdani, tussar, matka, Banglar Muslin, Nakshi Kantha, Santiniketan Batik), silk production, Handloom Census and Tantuja (plan: 15 Dec)

New lesson: Bengal's other industries — Bantala leather, Howrah foundries and GRSE, Haldia Petrochemicals, hosiery and garments, gems and jewellery, rice, potato and fish ranks, ASI factory figures, Directorate of Industries vs Directorate of MSME (plan: 14 Dec)

Tea corrected: orthodox/CTC are ways of making tea, black/green/white/oolong are types; Darjeeling = orthodox, mainly black (some green, white, oolong), 87 GI gardens; Dooars–Terai ≈99% of WB tea, mostly CTC, no GI; latest Tea Board shares; Kolkata (1861) and Siliguri (1976) auctions; flushes

GIs updated from the official registry: 59 registered (3rd in India), 24 added in 2025-26 incl. Murshidabad Silk, Sholapith, Bankura conch shell, Khagra bell metal, Natungram doll; district tables now show each district's sarees and craft GIs
Also added: Tropic of Cancer districts (asked in IDO 2019), Falta as an Export Processing Zone, Bengal Global Business Summit (history), Directorate of MSME's official name, Synergy
Computers rewritten in the simple style, with port numbers and IT Act penalties added; Section 66A note corrected (removed from the Act in 2023)

West Bengal industry, Safety & pollution, and Environment & energy: all 27 lessons rewritten in the simple style: one idea per part, starting from a real Bengal scene (a jute mill, a Dooars tea garden, a Kolkata market fire, a brick kiln), with numbers and sections in small tables, a 'Remember for the exam' box and a quick check after every part
Long lessons split into short parts: pollution science is now 24 bite-size parts, WB geography 16, Indian economy 15, Factories Act and OSH Code 13
Every fact, number, date, section and threshold kept exactly as checked before; independent checkers compared each lesson with the original item by item and re-solved every question

Small corrections found on the way: MSME 45-day tax rule (s.43B(h)) dated correctly as AY 2024-25, WBIIDC's 18 parks wording made consistent, Eastern Freight Corridor end point, bio-medical blue box per the 2018 amendment, Factories Act night-work rule for women
English: the six older lessons rewritten in the simple style (one rule per part, ✓/✗ examples, a tip and a quick check every part)
New lesson: Sentence transformation (voice, narration, simple/compound/complex, questions and tags, conjunctions like no sooner…than, degrees of comparison), in your plan on day 20
Tenses lesson now covers modals and 'if' sentences; one-word substitution adds 37 exam favourites (psephologist, obstetrician, regicide family, apiary, epicure, xenophobia…)
All of it independently checked: every answer re-solved and every MCQ confirmed to have exactly one right option

Physical Science rewritten in the simple style: all 11 lessons now teach one idea per part, starting from everyday things (a Digha beach, a fuse, curd, a rainbow), with plain-word explanations, a 'Remember for the exam' box and a quick check after every part
Physics numericals now taught like the maths chapters: one type per part with step tables
Inventions and units fact pack turned into clean tables
Every fact and number independently checked against the original lessons and standard textbooks (about 25 wording and precision fixes, no wrong answers found)
If your name isn't showing (phones unlocked before 24 Nov), Today now shows a 'Re-enter code' button; enter your code once and your name appears in the greeting and the watermark
Your name now appears faintly across every screen, so a shared screenshot shows whose copy it is
Basic copy protection: text can't be selected, copied or long-pressed outside text boxes (typing and search still work)
All maths chapters rewritten in the simple style you approved: HCF/LCM, percentage and profit, ratio and averages, speed and trains, interest and areas, equations
One idea per part, examples as small step tables, a quick check after every part, shortcuts only after the method
Every example and question re-solved by an independent checker (2 quick-check fixes, a few clearer rules)

Time and work, rewritten to be simple: one idea per part (pretend the job is pieces, add pieces per day), every example in a small table, a check after each part, shortcuts only after the method. No heavy formulas.
Fixed: with বাংলা on, long Bengali names (like the Jute Packaging Materials Act) pushed the page off the screen; they now wrap
Wide tables (rivers, units, organic groups) now scroll sideways inside the table instead of widening the page
New: বাংলা for the interview (More → বাংলা). Exact Bengali names of 1,357 key terms, e.g. tossa jute = তোষা পাট, white jute = সাদা পাট (দেশি পাট)
Tap বাংলা on any lesson to see the Bengali name beside each key term; tap a name for other names, a note and its pronunciation
Bengali term cards with Bengali voice and spoken answers; 40 interview answers in spoken Bengali; reading, writing and translation practice
Everything was checked by independent reviewers; official names follow the West Bengal government's own Bengali, e.g. ক্ষুদ্র, ছোট ও মাঝারি শিল্প ও বস্ত্র দফতর
Listen now follows bite-size reading: it reads only the part on screen, then says 'End of part 2 of 6' and waits
Tap Next part and it reads the next part by itself; tap Stop listening to end it. With Show all on, it reads the whole lesson
📝 Spoken script shows just the current part

Listen now reads like a teacher: ₹1,98,451 is 'one lakh ninety-eight thousand … rupees', km/h is 'kilometres per hour', 1/6 is 'one-sixth', A:B is 'A is to B', H₂SO₄ is 'H 2 S O 4', dates as '1st July'
Memory tricks, exam traps, tips and quick-check answers are announced, read slower and followed by a pause; quick checks pause so you can answer first
📝 Spoken script on each lesson shows exactly what will be read and highlights the line being spoken
Checked on the whole course: every number keeps its exact value; two independent reviews of 600 lines
Indian-English voices (🇮🇳) are now chosen first automatically; they say Hooghly, Haldia and Bhabishyat correctly
With an American or British voice, about 330 Indian names in the course are respelled before reading (Haldia → 'Huldiya', Rishra → 'Rishraa'); the screen still shows the normal spelling
Formulas with n (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, (1 + R/100)ⁿ) no longer show boxes on phones; they're drawn as proper subscripts and powers everywhere
Read aloud says them properly too ('to the power n')
Big figures are now shown the way you'd remember them: per-capita GSDP 'about ₹1.98 lakh, roughly ₹2 lakh', GSDP 'about ₹21.5 lakh crore', with the exact figure in brackets
Say answer accepts a close figure (within 2%) for 'about' numbers and money amounts, marked ≈ close enough; years, codes and definitions must still be exact
Say answer: 'sixth' now matches 6th, numbers with commas (2,000 / 1,98,451) and spoken units (megawatt, pascal, kilometre) match, and one-word answers like prepositions work
Tested on all 1,706 flashcards: saying the exact answer is always accepted
Say answer now checks each part of the answer separately and shows it: ticked parts you said, dashed parts you missed, and any wrong number you said
Getting the main part right (e.g. 'Rishra' for Rishra, Hooghly, 1855) now counts as partly right instead of wrong
Reading voice (More → Reading voice, or 'Voice' on flashcards): the app now picks the most natural voice on your device, and you can test and choose any voice and set the speed
Flashcards can listen: tap 🎤 Say answer, speak, and the app shows the answer, checks what you said and suggests a rating
Numbers must match exactly (1897 is not 1899); spoken years and dates like 'eighteen ninety seven' are understood
Flashcards can speak: tap 🔊 Read aloud, or turn on Auto-read to hear the question, then the answer when you reveal it
Listen to lessons now also works in the GitHub copy, using your device's voice
14 new lessons from a coverage audit of every past-paper question, each independently fact-checked:
English: Word power (370 exam words with meaning, synonym and antonym), Sentence completion and cloze, Prepositions and fixed pairs (142 pairs, 45 phrasal verbs)
Maths and reasoning: Equations and word problems, Seating arrangement and puzzles, Statement–conclusion and assumptions, Venn counting and letter tasks
Science: Physics numericals workshop, Radioactivity and the EM spectrum, Inventions and units fact pack
WB industry: West Bengal geography, Indian economy essentials, Bengal's industrial firsts. Pollution: Pollution science (water, air, waste, toxic diseases)
Study plan rebuilt for about 4 hours a day: every lesson is now scheduled by 25 December, leaving January for mocks and revision
Flashcards: 30 new cards a day (choose 15, 30 or 50)

Six maths workshops for competitive-exam arithmetic: HCF and LCM; percentage and profit; ratio, averages and ages; time and work; speed and trains; interest and mensuration. Method first, 8 worked examples each, 15 graded questions. Added to your plan from today.
Two new chemistry lessons: organic chemistry made simple, and chemistry in industry and daily life (common names, alloys, ores, cement, fertilisers)
All new lessons independently checked: every number recomputed and every fact verified
Daily recall is now a 10-question recall test on the previous day's lessons. It uses bank questions you haven't seen yet, then any you got wrong, and ticks itself when you finish.

Work ahead: once today's plan is done, tap Work ahead and Today shows the next day's full plan. Tick everything there, revision and mocks included, and it counts for that day. The Study plan shows how many days ahead you are and your new finish date.
Doubt search: tap any match to jump straight to that part of the lesson; it's highlighted when you land
Ask Claude now asks before taking you out of the app
Search ignores filler words, so the matches are sharper

Ask a doubt now searches the whole course as you type: lessons, key facts, exam traps, question explanations, past papers and interview notes. Most doubts are answered instantly, without leaving the app.
The app now greets you by name
New access-code page that shows what's inside the course
Study plan: a day now shows ✓ only when everything planned for it is done. A lesson read ahead of schedule shows ◐ (lesson done, the rest of that day still to do).

Time-trap mode: 119 hard, independently checked questions. About 12 in every 100 are mixed into full, half and quick mocks at random (switch on from your second full mock). They are revealed only after you submit.

New 'Where your time went' report after every mock: time per section against the fair share, your 5 slowest questions, how you handled each time trap, questions you never reached, and your trend across mocks
Deep check by 8 independent reviewers: every visual, every slider formula, consistency across lessons/flashcards/questions/interview notes, and all app scoring maths

Fixed facts: Bhabishyat age 18–55; GI mangoes are all Malda; OSH Code safety officer at 500+ workers (250+ hazardous); Eastern DFC runs to Sonnagar today, Andal is the planned end; CESC formed 1897, supply from 1899
Fixed rules stated too broadly: dice 'matching positions', 'some' in syllogisms, false weights (at cost price only), fraction HCF/LCM (lowest terms first), neither…nor, lest, between/among
Fixed visuals: compound-interest gap formula, prohibition-sign bar direction, mandatory sign, policy timeline order, thermometer scale, ETP stages, noise exposure table, Ohm's law rounding

Fixed app maths: half and quick mocks now keep the exam's section split; practice counts include bank questions; retries no longer inflate accuracy; untagged mock answers shown separately in the guessing coach; 'Best full mock'; marks-at-risk needs enough answers; an unfinished mock survives a reload
Past-papers notes corrected (counts, cut-off source, English advice)
All 377 past-paper answers re-solved blind by independent checkers: 370 agreed, 1 answer corrected (IDO 2019 Q33, India's top trading partner in 2018-19 was the USA), 6 explanations clarified
Interview prep updated from the official advertisement: Bengali ability is essential and may be tested at the interview; qualifying marks on the 115 total by category; tie-break by age
Fixed: Export backup now works in the claude.ai app
239 past questions from WBCS Prelims and Mains (2016–2023) that fit the IDO syllabus, grouped by section under Past papers; every answer re-solved and independently checked
Outdated facts in old papers are flagged in the explanation (e.g. leaded petrol ban)
Question bank: 979 new fact-checked questions across all 7 sections (each set reviewed independently; every calculation recomputed)
Real mocks: full 100-question mock weighted like the exam, plus half, quick and section tests; questions you haven't seen come first
Guessing coach: tag each answer sure / half-sure / guess and see which kind earns or loses you marks
Speed drills at exam pace (practice tab)
Crash revision: sections ranked by marks at risk, printable cheat sheets, rapid-revision quiz
Interview prep (15 marks): likely questions, fact-checked answer outlines, 90-second timed practice
Corrected: the Dankuni–Surat freight corridor passes through Jharkhand (per the May 2026 gazette); OSH Central Rules' age-40 check-up applies to centrally regulated sectors
Fixed: the Next part button no longer sits under the Ask a doubt button on phones
Bite-size reading: every lesson now opens one part at a time, with a progress bar, time left and a nudge every two parts (tap "Show all" to read it in one go)
Games in every lesson: a match-the-pairs game before the recap, "Play: put these in order" on every timeline, and "Test me: hide the numbers" on every ladder and fact card set

22 new drawn and interactive visuals: fire triangle, safety signs, bio-medical bins, gas cylinders, Heinrich's dots, hierarchy pyramid, effluent tanks, thermometers, prism, circuits, sodium atom, and sliders for pH, temperature, Ohm's law, km/h, fan and wind power, interest and clock angles
A small celebration when you finish a lesson
New drawn visuals (samples): the Factories Act as a building (lesson 2.1), a noise meter with a slider (2.2), and the NFPA diamond drawn in its real colours (2.5)
Progress now shows how many questions you've tried out of how many are available, overall and for each section, with a progress bar and the section's exam marks
Accuracy now shows the count too, e.g. "39 of 42"
Module 7 reviewed with every calculation re-worked (about 315 items; all 100 answer keys correct)

Fixed: 1/7 = 14.29%; clock angle over 180° → use 360° minus it; mirror clock for 11:00–12:59 uses 23:60 − time; scaling a cylinder's radius alone gives 4× volume, not 8×; an odd-one-out question with two defensible answers replaced
The whole course (48 lessons, 473 questions) has now been independently checked
Module 6 English reviewed (about 305 items; all answer keys correct)
Fixed: a/an letter list now includes H, vowels and the U exception (an HR manager, a UPSC exam); agree with/to/on; consist of vs consist in; four questions reworded so only one option can be defended
Module 5 fact-checked (about 165 items; all answer keys and shortcuts correct)
Added: HEC-2M at ISI Kolkata (1955) was the first computer installed in India; DPDP Rules notified 13 Nov 2025 with main duties from 13 May 2027; Section 66A was struck down (2015), not repealed
Module 4 fact-checked (about 340 claims; all answer keys, formulas and worked examples correct)
Clarified: Indian wiring colours (red live, black neutral, green earth; brown/blue on flexible cords), rainbow = refraction + dispersion + internal reflection, light slows in optically denser media
Module 3 fact-checked (about 270 claims, all 56 answer keys correct); fixes and additions made
Added: India's 2035 additional carbon sink of 3.5–4 bn t; COP31 led by Türkiye with Australia presiding over negotiations; Khavda now India's largest renewable park
Corrected: tiger is a secondary consumer in grass → deer → tiger; GWP values labelled IPCC AR5; CESC formed 1897, first power station 1899
Modules 1 and 2 fact-checked by independent reviewers (about 820 claims and 171 answer keys); 30-plus corrections made

Key fixes: deep-sea port moved from Tajpur to Dadanpatrabar (June 2026); Banglashree expired, not revoked; CPCB Blue category is for municipal waste services (CETPs stay Red); crèche is for more than 30 women; WB is 2nd in MSMEs after UP (national survey); 59 GI tags
Added OSH Code welfare thresholds (canteen 100+, crèche more than 50 workers, welfare officer 250+) and the 2016 CPCB bands
